messages:
sophie: quick sync — noticed inconsistent abort/cancel behavior across SDKs when streaming + token refresh. Node abort early, python sometimes hangs, Go cancels but server keeps sending. Can we align on expected semantics?

rahul: observed same on prod canary. repro: start streaming, rotate auth mid-stream, then call AbortController.abort() on client. node stops immediately, but python client waits for server eof.

leo: can you paste minimal repro? also what should server do when client cancels but auth refresh occurs?

rahul: minimal Node snippet: ```js
const ac = new AbortController();
fetch(url, { signal: ac.signal, headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } })
 // streaming reader...
ac.abort(); // immediate stop, close socket
```
python variant: ```py
with client.stream(... ) as stream:
    # token refresh happens in background
    stream.cancel()  # our wrapper uses asyncio.CancelledError
```
python process sometimes awaits remaining chunks before returning.

maya: I think difference is lower-level: Node's fetch closes the socket; our python wrapper drains/awaits generator cleanup which waits for server to finish send+flush. Go uses context.Context cancel which closes request but server might still be writing for a bit.

sophie: desired cross-sdk contract proposal: 1) client abort should close local read+write (no more processing), surface a consistent cancel error to caller; 2) server should best-effort stop generation on noticing connection close, but may still finish an in-flight token; 3) if auth refresh happens concurrently, client should not auto-retry the same streaming request — retries only allowed for idempotent non-streaming calls. Thoughts?

leo: +1 on no auto-retry for streaming. For SDKs we need documented semantics and an explicit api: e.g., `stream.cancel()` returns immediately and raises CancelledError/AbortError consistently.

rahul: implementation notes: Node: already uses AbortController -> good. Python: change stream.cancel() to call transport.close() then raise CancelledError without awaiting drain. Need to ensure we don't leak background tasks.

maya: Go: ensure context cancel closes body reader and returns ctx.Err() quickly. Might need a small change in our http client wrapper to call resp.Body.CloseWithError(...) when ctx cancelled.

dev-bot: deploy check: create GH issue and run cross-sdk e2e matrix (node, python, go) on canary.

sophie: action items: @rahul open GH issue with repro + suggested python fix; @leo draft SDK contract doc (short) and canonical error codes mapping; @maya prototype Go body close tweak. I'll own rollout plan and release notes.

rahul: on it — will include token-rotation scenario and link to logs (we saw 504s when server kept producing).

leo: quick question — should `stream.cancel()` be sync or async in py SDK? prefer sync to be immediate, but will need to ensure underlying tasks are cancelled.

maya: sync API makes sense for ergonomics. We can have `await stream.aclose()` for graceful close if the user wants to wait for server ack. Default cancel should be immediate.

sophie: love that. let's add a short example to docs: ```py
# immediate cancel
stream.cancel()  # raises CancelledError
# graceful close if you care
await stream.aclose()  # attempts polite shutdown, may wait
```

rahul: testing plan: add unit tests that simulate mid-stream auth refresh and assert no auto-retry and proper cancellation error surfaced. also test memory/leak by running many cancels in loop.

dev-bot: GH Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/987 — triage label added.

sophie: thanks all. ping me in-thread when PRs are ready. I'll update release notes and console docs. :thumbsup:

leo: will do. small follow-up: do we need server-side timeout config to expedite cancellation detection? could add short TCP-level keepalive, but that's infra.

maya: opened infra ticket for keepalive tuning, referencing GH #987.

sophie: ok closing this sync — tracked in GH #987, next check-in Friday.
